sources.title: Physics-informed PointNet: A deep learning solver for steady-state incompressible flows and thermal fields on multiple sets of irregular geometries
sources.version_note: arXiv v2, 27 Oct 2022; PDF creation metadata D:20221028011705Z
findings: Section 4.2 uses 135 generated geometries: 108 in Phi (train) and 27 in Psi (test); point clouds are subsets of finite-element mesh vertices.

Section 4.2 says: 'Note that no boundary condition is specified for the pressure in the loss function (Eq. 39).' This is the natural-convection inverse case, not the Section 4.1 manufactured-solution pressure BC.
Section 4.2 says the sparse data and inquiry-point validation use 'one of our high fidelity finite-element numerical solvers already used in the literature [34, 29, 28, 30, 31]'.
Section 4.1.2 separately studies a manufactured-solution pressure boundary condition; that condition must not be transplanted to Section 4.2.
Section 4.2 reports noisy/absent pressure-observation sensitivity but does not record a pressure gauge, reference node, zero-mean rule, or output re-scaling.
sources.why_not: the paper names a class of in-house solvers but not the generating version, pressure gauge, reference node, or output postprocessing; no corresponding data-generation code was found

sources.readme_version: README says Version 1.0; alternative/README.md documents installation and data download
findings: The public repository contains the PIPN training/implementation script, not a data generator or FEM solver.
alternative/README.md step 5 states the dataset is a public NumPy array downloaded from https://web.stanford.edu/~kashefi/data/HeatTransferData.npy.
No pressure-gauge, solver-version, mesh, or generation-parameter file is present in the public tree.

sources.finding: the public distribution is byte-identical to the local canonical HeatTransferData.npy; this identifies the data distribution but not the historical solver gauge

sources.type: arXiv paper cited by PIPN as one of the in-house FEM solver family
sources.title: A coarse grid projection method for accelerating heat transfer computations
sources.author: Ali Kashefi
findings: The paper describes a semi-implicit unstructured-triangular finite-element CGP version and pressure Poisson step.
It is an algorithmic/family reference, not a record that the exact 135-geometry dataset was generated by this version.
No public code or 135-geometry generation record identified.

synthesis.mathematical_note: the pressure enters the incompressible equations only through its gradient; p+C with the same velocity/temperature is an equivalent solution. Without a recorded anchor condition, C is not uniquely recoverable from the equations or the stored fields.
